title: Dominic and the Protocol
premise: Ulyana Thackeray, navigator of the freighter Dominic, discovers that the colony on Verity's Landing—officially evacuated years ago—is still alive and slowly dying of a reactor failure no fleet will acknowledge. The unfamiliar name on the manifest of the never-flown ship Meridian belongs to a colonist who was secretly ferried out as proof of life, and his existence is the linchpin of a fragile truce between two rival fleets. When Ulyana exposes the truth to save the colony, she risks shattering the lie that keeps the fleets from open war. In the end she chooses truth over loyalty, testifying before both fleets with the colonist at her side; the war is averted not by the lie but by the shame of the revealed record, and the colony is finally rescued.
about_author: Sable Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to ships talk to each other across empty water. They write science fiction about people who keep records, and about what those records cost them.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. During a routine run aboard the Dominic, Ulyana audits the cargo manifest and finds the impossible: a passenger listed on the Meridian, a ship decommissioned before it ever flew. She cross-checks old logs and realizes the 'evacuated' colony of Verity's Landing sent out one living witness—and then went silent. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the moment a professional discovers her profession has been used to bury something.

chapters.title: What the Truce Is Made Of
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with an interlude from Captain Osei of the rival fleet. Ulyana confronts the Dominic's owner, who reveals the witness's existence anchors a truce: each fleet believes the other holds the proof of the colony's fate. Speaking up means war. Osei's interlude shows him manufacturing evidence to preserve the same lie. The beat is complicity—Ulyana realizes everyone decent she knows is keeping the secret.

chapters.title: Verity's Landing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Defying orders, she diverts the Dominic to the colony and finds two hundred survivors rationing a failing reactor, led by the witness's sister, who recorded everything for years. Fleet patrols close in as her unauthorized course is detected. The climax arrives when both fleets converge on the colony, weapons hot, each believing the other stole their hostage-proof. The beat is terror transfigured into resolve as Ulyana broadcasts the colony's full archive to both flagships.

chapters.title: The Record
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, closing with Osei's surrender of his forged files. Facing a joint tribunal, Ulyana argues that the lie held peace only by making both fleets liars together; the colony's own recordings, unedited, do the rest. The witness's sister addresses the assembly. The fleets stand down, rescue ships launch, and Ulyana is stripped of her certification but given the colony's gratitude. The beat is costly vindication: truth wins, but not cleanly, and she carries the weight of what it nearly broke.
